results.summary_before: Whisk is a 16-bit serial RISC CPU that executes instructions from up to 64 kilobytes of external SPI SRAM. It uses a single SPI interface for instruction fetch, loads, and stores, and internally operates in a fully serial manner to match the SPI memory throughput. An optional IO port interface provides up to 16 outputs and 8 inputs using shift registers. The design requires a host board with SPI SRAM and a host interface for loading programs, and it is notable for its compact serial architecture.

results.summary_before: This project implements the 2048 sliding tile puzzle game in Verilog with VGA video output and optional SNES-compatible gamepad input. Players move tiles using the ui_in buttons or a Gamepad Pmod, and the design includes a start animation, two color themes, and a unit test mode with debug pins. It requires a TinyVGA Pmod for display and optionally a Gamepad Pmod for controller input. The design is notable for fitting a complete graphical game with input handling and debug support into a 2x2 tile area.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit segmented mismatch-shaping R2R DAC encoder that takes digital input and produces a set of output bits that can be summed with specific weights to reconstruct the analog value. It operates in four modes: first-order mismatch shaping with dither, randomization, first-order shaping without dither, and static encoding, selectable via input pins. Testing requires an external resistor ladder and capacitor to create the analog output voltage, and the design is free-running off the project clock. The encoder is notable for its mismatch-shaping techniques aimed at improving DAC linearity, though it requires careful external component selection for optimal performance.
